chains.title: The T allele strengthens HOXB13 binding and RFX6 enhancer activity
chains.element: A regulatory element within the RFX6 locus containing rs339331
chains.cell_type: Androgen-responsive prostate luminal epithelial cells, including LNCaP

links.claim: The ref T allele is hypothesized to bind HOXB13 more strongly than alt C. HOXB13 is the leading candidate based on prior reports concerning this locus; no occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here to establish the allele effect.
The rs339331-containing sequence acts as a regulatory element whose activity is increased by stronger HOXB13 binding.
This regulatory effect occurs in androgen-responsive prostate luminal epithelial cells such as LNCaP.
Increased RFX6 expression in prostate cells contributes to increased prostate cancer susceptibility.

predictions: In heterozygous cells, HOXB13 occupancy at rs339331 is enriched on the T allele.
The T allele is associated with greater enhancer activity and RFX6 expression than the C allele in prostate cells.
falsified_if: A well-powered allele-specific HOXB13 occupancy assay shows no T-allele enrichment or shows greater occupancy on C.
The rs339331 alleles have no reproducible difference in enhancer activity or RFX6 expression in relevant prostate cells.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs339331
predictions: There is no reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy or regulatory effect attributable to rs339331.
Any prostate cancer association at the locus is due to linkage with another causal variant, a non-TF mechanism, or chance.
falsified_if: Editing rs339331 alone reproducibly changes TF occupancy and enhancer activity in relevant prostate cells, with a corresponding change in target-gene expression.

chains.title: The C allele changes FOXA1 binding and alters RFX6 regulation
chains.element: A regulatory element within the RFX6 locus containing rs339331
chains.cell_type: Androgen-responsive prostate luminal epithelial cells, including LNCaP

links.claim: As an alternative to the HOXB13 model, the alt C allele is hypothesized to bind FOXA1 more strongly; this is speculative, and no FOXA1 occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied here.
Allele-dependent FOXA1 binding changes the activity of the rs339331-containing regulatory element.
The altered element changes RFX6 expression.
The effect occurs in androgen-responsive prostate luminal epithelial cells such as LNCaP.
The resulting change in RFX6 expression modifies prostate cancer susceptibility.

predictions: In heterozygous cells, FOXA1 occupancy at rs339331 is enriched on the C allele, without the T-specific HOXB13 enrichment predicted by H1.
The C allele produces a FOXA1-dependent change in enhancer activity and RFX6 expression.
falsified_if: Allele-specific assays show no C-enriched FOXA1 occupancy or show stronger FOXA1 occupancy on T.
FOXA1 perturbation does not affect the allele-dependent enhancer or RFX6 expression difference.

matrix.test: Allele-specific HOXB13 CUT&RUN-qPCR across rs339331 in heterozygous LNCaP cells

outcomes.outcome: HOXB13 occupancy is enriched on the ref T allele.
No T-enriched HOXB13 occupancy is expected; FOXA1, rather than HOXB13, is the proposed allele-sensitive TF.
No reproducible allele-specific HOXB13 occupancy is expected.

next_experiment: Perform allele-specific HOXB13 CUT&RUN-qPCR across rs339331 in heterozygous LNCaP cells. T-enriched occupancy would support the leading HOXB13 chain over the null; no allele-specific enrichment would weaken it. If LNCaP is not heterozygous at this site, use matched T/C isogenic cells.
